F‑Droid 2.0 finally gives Android the open‑source app store it’s been missing.

The new release rewrites the client in Kotlin, adds a sandboxed installer, and introduces a metadata‑driven review pipeline that can reject malicious binaries before they reach users. For developers, the built‑in CI integration means a single push can publish a new version across all supported devices, cutting release friction dramatically.

What stands out to me is the shift from a “catalog” mindset to a “trusted marketplace” model. By cryptographically signing every index entry and enforcing reproducible builds, F‑Droid is turning the old fear of “unvetted APKs” into a concrete security guarantee—something Google Play has struggled to articulate.

I’m curious: will you start testing your next Android release on F‑Droid 2.0, or keep it as a niche fallback?  

#Android #OpenSource #AppSecurity #DevOps #FOSS
